questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Heidelberg is a very beautiful city with an interesting history and buildings. Their university is also known to be very good and as I had never been to southern Germany, that was also a motivation for me to choose Heidelberg.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, although I experienced some bureaucratical/practical challenges, e.g. regarding insurance and getting documents signed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance from Studierendenwerk (The organisation responsible for all things about your study, except the study itself). They gave us a very detailed guide to how to do different things. Also at the first in our intro week at the university we received a lot of different guides about the city and how to do things regarding our study/courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was pretty satisfied, but in regards to information about different courses, I did not get enough help or guidance, in which as a result, I chose one course at Master Level although I am still studying for my bachelor degree. This course was a bit harder for me, and it would have been nice to be better informed on beforehand, which courses are directed/meant for Bachelor students and which ones for Master Students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We could choose from a lot of different rooms in WGS (Collectives) - both in the centralpart of the city and in other parts of the city. I was very lucky and got into a very central placed WG, only 10 minutes away from where my courses took place.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a little shared kitchen in our WG. It was possible to cook, but there wasn't a lot of space. The Canteen at the university was very nice with good and varied food and relatively cheap prices:))

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That not all furniture, cutlery, vacuum cleaner etc. are available in the housing. Sometimes you will have to buy new things/extra things that are not there. Also that it is mandatory in germany to pay "Rundfunksteuer" and remember to talk with your roommates about that and make an agreement about it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process partly took place online, where I had to send personal information to the University (Picture of myself, date of birth, my earlier studies, information about insurance) and then the responsible persons had to sign different documents, e.g. Enrollment. When I arrived in Germany, I had to fill in more information online, to be able to get my Student Card. I also had to announce that I had moved to the city at the city council.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an institute that only works with helping international students. It was possible to contact them over email or physically in the central part of town. Apart from that, an employee from Studierendenwerk and two from the university had a mail correspondence with all Erasmus students, to help and inform us about things we had to do and answer questions. They were all very nice and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I got accepted into all the courses for which I had applied.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check your Ku Mail, as you will be reminded about steps you have to do in mobility online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am currently taking my bachelors degree and I were as well, when I was doing my exchange. Most of my courses except one course (that were on Masters Level) were on Bachelor level and three of my courses were specifically aimed at Erasmus students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit more formal than at UCPH and all exams were written in hand with no accommodations (Notes, computer porgrammes) available. That was a very different experience for me, as at UCPH exams normally take place digitally and you may bring your notes, use digital programmes etc. as help. ECTS points are also granted in a much different way. In Denmark it is very fixed from the beginning, but in Germany it was much more "flexible" - meaning that you could make an agreement with your teacher about how many ECTS you wanted/needed, and then write an assignment according to that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Grammatik im Kontakt
Grundlagen Spracherwerb
Wortschatz C2
Textverstehen und Textproduktion B2
Konversation in Kleingruppen B2
Gegenwartsdramatik im Kontext des 42. Heidelberger Stückemarkts
Die französischen Revolution und Napoleon in der deutschsprachigen Literatur

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the courses at IDF that are specifically aimed at Erasmus students, since it was very nice to get to know people from other countries and their culture and languages and it was very relevant topics in regards to improving my German, written as well as spoken/oral proficiency.
I would also recommend the course "Grammatik im Kontakt", as we were a lot of students with mixed backgrounds and the combination with grammar/Contact between languages made the course very relevant and super interesting. The course "Gegenwartsdramatik im Kontext des 42. Heidelberger Stückemarkts" was also super interesting. It was interesting to learn about a current literary/cultural event taking place in the city and we were invited to see the theatre and hear interviews with the autors behind the plays, which was also very nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Rundfunksteuer. (German tax for radio and television)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a little bit more expensive than I thought. Housing were way less expensive than I expected, before finding my housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of different sports activities were available via Hochschulsport. They had Kayak classes, hiking, ballet etc. Apart from sport, they also offered two choices. It was free for students to visit the theatre and the prices for cinema tickets were reduced.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choir. You get to know a lot of new people and it is fun to sing. Also groups for finding friends/meeting new people in the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sail on the Neckar, visit the old castle. Go to the cinema or on museum. There is also a lot of opportunities for hiking in nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. germany is a lot like Denmark. The only little thing that is different, is that they are generally a bit more formal than Danes typically are.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is normal to have a more formal relationship with your teachers, e.g. not calling them by their first name, but last name. I found that a bit difficult sometimes, as I am not so accustomed to it. Apart from that I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like German literature and food, and the people are a lot like danish people, which makes it very easy to fit in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the university system is more unstructured than at UCPH, and that you may need to ask more questions/to ask more for help in general, to make sure that everything is at should be. It is a good idea to think about transport (If you want to buy the Germany ticket), e.g. if you have plans to visit your family during your stay or just want to visit and explore more of germany while being on Erasmus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No:))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have gotten way better at speaking German as well as understanding it by attending classes only in German and by living surrounded by people only speaking German to me, to a point where I am almost fluent in understanding the language. It feels as if I have "gained" a new language In a very short amount of time, and it is a very good skill to have acquired. I have learned a lot about the beautiful city of Heidelberg (where I was at exchange) and it feels a bit like my second home now - that is also a very rewarding part of my exchange experience. I have gotten to know a lot of new people and had classes and courses that were very interesting and where I read a lot of interesting literature and learned many interesting and useful things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To live alone so far away from home (10 Hours by train). I have always lived in Copenhagen and I lived with my family before my exchange. Having to balance practical things, being social and preparing for university classes in a foreign country was a little challenging in the beginning and from time to time during my exchange, but I have gotten a lot more independent and learned that it is possible to manage it, even though I was sometimes a little scared.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
